# Generated-site tells

Each of these is legitimate when a brief calls for it. They become a problem when they appear by default, whatever the subject. If one shows up in your output, you need a reason specific to Nirmaan, and the reason goes in `docs/DESIGN.md`.

## Palette and surface

- **Warm cream background with a high-contrast serif and a terracotta accent.** Very common in current generated design.
- **Near-black background with one acid-green or vermilion accent.** The other common default for "technical" sites.
- **Gradient washes, glow blobs, glassmorphism.** Decoration that says nothing about the work.
- **Tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) used as black.** Fine in moderation. As a reflex it is a tell.

Instead: choose 4-6 named colors that come from the subject (see the brief), and test the palette in both a light and a dark context before committing.

## Layout

- **Content chopped into identical rounded cards** with the same radius and the same soft grey shadow.
- **Hero = big headline + subtitle + two buttons + stat row.** The stat row is the strongest tell, especially with invented numbers.
- **Everything centered**, every section the same height, same vertical rhythm.
- **Broadsheet layout** (hairline rules, zero radius, dense columns) used because it looks "editorial".

Instead: let the content set the layout. A case study is a long read with a sticky outline. A project index is a ranked list, not a grid of equal tiles.

## Typography and labels

- **Tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow above every heading.**
- **One word in the headline italicised or colored** for emphasis.
- **Meta strings joined with middle dots** ("Python · FastAPI · Postgres").
- **"WORD - fragment" labels** with a spaced em dash.
- **Monospace for every small label** as a shortcut to "technical".
- **A "→" appended to every link and button.**
- **Numbered 01 / 02 / 03 markers** on content that is not a sequence.

Instead: use sentence case, label only what needs labelling, and use monospace where content is actually code, identifiers, or data.

## Motion

- Fade-and-slide-up on every section as it scrolls into view.
- Hover lift or glow on every card.
- Looping decorative animation, parallax, or cursor effects.

Instead: one deliberate moment, and motion that answers a user action.

## Content

- "Passionate engineer", "building the future", "cutting-edge", "seamless", "leverage", "robust", "end-to-end solutions".
- Invented metrics ("reduced latency by 70%") or testimonials.
- Lists of skills as logos or progress bars.
- Placeholder copy such as lorem ipsum or "Your amazing project here".

Instead: concrete nouns and verbs, real numbers with context, or an honest placeholder the owner can see.

## Process tells

- Stopping after the first working version without looking at it on a phone.
- Adding every shadcn component "in case".
- Leaving the preset font and radius untouched.
